No propositions came through with your message, so I can't choose from a list. If you mean the general case, I'd argue the most powerful refutation is that pleasures and pains can't be measured on one common scale, since that undermines the calculus's core step of summing units of pleasure (the point Mill pressed with his qualitative distinction between higher and lower pleasures). Paste the options and I'll pick the strongest one and explain why.
